add.event: 密歇根州宣布八天银行假日
add.evidence: Beginning on February 14, 1933, Michigan, an industrial state that had been hit particularly hard by the Great Depression in the United States, declared an eight-day bank holiday.

add.event: 银行重新开业，储户排队将现金存回
add.evidence: When the institutions reopened for business on March 13, 1933, depositors stood in line to return their stashed cash to neighborhood banks.

add.event: 华尔街复市首日道指涨15.34%至62.10点
add.evidence: On March 15, 1933, the first day of stock trading after the extended closure of Wall Street, the Dow Jones Industrial Average, gaining 8.26 points to close at 62.10; a gain of 15.34%.

add.event: 罗斯福签署第6102号行政令，禁止私人持有货币黄金
add.evidence: on April 5, 1933, President Roosevelt signed Executive Order 6102 criminalizing the possession of monetary gold
